title: stale org->project mapping cache causes billing bleed after project rename
creator: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary:

An intermittent bug in the org->project attribution cache causes ingress events to be billed to the parent org (or to the wrong project) after a project rename or idempotent key rebind. The root cause appears to be a stale in-memory mapper used by the metering proxy fallback path; when a project name/alias update races with token exchange, requests are processed with an outdated mapping and end up recorded against the wrong billing entity.

Impact:
- Multiple customers reported sudden billing spikes and incorrect per-project usage in the last 48 hours.
- Affected requests show correct API key but wrong project_id in aggregated metering records.
- Severity: P0 — actively misbilling production traffic and causing invoices to be incorrect.

Reproduction (observed in staging and in one customer repro):
1) Create project P-A and issue API key K.
2) Start heavy streaming workload (10–50 RPS) using K.
3) Rename project to P-B (rename operation updates catalog and fires rewrite event).
4) Concurrently rotate API key (token aliasing flow) or rebind key to a subproject.
5) Metering proxy receives requests and consults in-memory org->project cache; race leaves cache stale for ~30s.
6) Metering writes usage rows labeled with the pre-rename project id (or default org) instead of the current project id.

Notable logs/traces (anonymized):
- metering-proxy: mapper_cache_miss=false cache_version=42 serving_project=proj_old
- catalog-watcher: published_version=43 project_rename=proj_old->proj_new
- usage-writer: write_success=true user_key_alias=abc123 recorded_project=proj_old

Initial triage findings:
- The cache is an in-process LRU with manual invalidation triggered only on catalog webhook success. Catalog updates occasionally arrive out-of-order vs the key rotation message queue (kafka partitioning mismatch).
- Fallback code path used during short catalog latencies bypasses the canonical resolver and reads the stale LRU.
- There is no defensive invariant in the ingestion pipeline to assert that the recorded_project matches the active mapping for the API key at write-time.

Proposed plan of action (multi-step):
1) Hotfix (1–2 day):
   - Add conservative server-side mitigation: if catalog_version != mapper_cache_version then reject non-idempotent writes with 409 and return a header X-Metering-Mapper-Stale: 1 so callers can retry. Implement as feature-flagged change behind ff/metering-mapper-strict.
   - Deploy to canary region and run synthetic repro load for 24h.
   - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/892 (WIP)

2) Root fix (2–3 sprints):
   - Replace process-local LRU with a strongly-consistent resolver backed by a read-through cache using the catalog's versioned key-value store (etcd) and a version token on each API key.
   - Ensure the mapper update path is idempotent and ordered by catalog event offsets; add event-sequencing in catalog-watcher so we never apply older versions after newer ones.
   - Add a short-lived immutable mapping token on API key creation/rotation so metering can validate recorded_project token at write-time.

3) Data repair and monitoring:
   - Backfill job to scan recent usage rows with recorded_project not matching canonical mapping and re-emit corrected usage events (will carry a correction_flag to avoid double billing). See migration script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/blob/main/fix-mapping-backfill.py
   - Add metric meter.attribution.orphaned_count and a Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-internal/d/usage/attribution-health

4) Tests and validation:
   - Unit tests for mapper ordering and catalog-watcher event application.
   - Integration test that performs rename+rotate under load and asserts 100% correct attribution.

Rollout plan:
- Step 0: Merge hotfix behind ff/metering-mapper-strict and enable on internal-only cluster. Run synthetic workload for 24h.
- Step 1: Canary rollout to US-west (10% of traffic) — monitor orphaned_count and invoice_delta.
- Step 2: Gradual rollout to production regional clusters over 48h if metrics stable.

Metrics to watch (alert thresholds):
- meter.attribution.orphaned_rate > 0.1% sustained for 15m -> Pager/SEV2
- invoice_delta anomalous increase > 5% for a single org -> Pager/SEV1
- catalog_watcher_lag > 5s -> Alert (ops)

Open questions / blockers:
- Does the billing pipeline idempotency allow us to safely re-emit corrected usage rows without double billing? (Finance/Revenue needs sign-off)
- Which catalog event ordering guarantees exist across clusters? Ops to confirm kafka partitioning by org key.
- Do we want to tolerate brief rejections (409) during catalog sync as opposed to best-effort attribution?

Immediate next steps (today):
- Marco: finish the hotfix PR and add header instrumentation (ETA: 2026-03-12) — in progress.
- Aisha: run synthetic repro and capture traces (ETA: 2026-03-12).
- Finance: schedule emergency review for the backfill semantics (requested).

Related artifacts and links:
- Repro harness: https://ci.redwood-internal/repro/ENG-44902/run/13
- Draft playbook for mitigation: https://confluence.redwood-internal/display/BILLING/ENG-44902+playbook
- Initial customer reports: drive link (internal) https://drive.redwood-internal/alerts/44902

If anyone with deeper catalog-watcher context (Kenji, Priya) can chime in on the ordering guarantees and whether we can atomically attach a version token to every key during rotation, that will unblock the root fix design.

Status updates: 
- 2026-03-11 09:47 (Aisha): Confirmed repro in staging with project rename + rotation. Captured traces and uploaded to repro job.
- 2026-03-11 16:20 (Marco): Pushed hotfix branch w/ header instrumentation and a basic catalog_version check; tests added for 409 path. PR opened (WIP).
- 2026-03-12 08:15 (Aisha): Canary enabled on internal cluster — no orphaned writes observed in first 6h.

Notes for follow-up: prioritize the root fix in the next billing-platform sprint; planning session scheduled for 2026-03-14 to scope the etcd-backed resolver and migration strategy.
